correctness.rationale: The three partial derivatives cannot vanish together at a projective point, so the plane quartic is geometrically smooth and integral of genus 3. Independently reproduced the extension counts with `python3 /workspace/review_evidence/quartic_replay.py`, rather than executing verify_curve.py. The replay uses F9 with eta^2=−1 and builds its quadratic and cubic extensions by rootless monic polynomials. For a nonzero right-hand side a, cyclicity of the multiplicative group gives four roots precisely when a^((9^m−1)/4)=1; the zero value contributes one root. Across m=1,2,3 the affine counts are 1,105,892 and the [x:1:0] chart contributes 0,4,0; [1:0:0] is excluded. The Frobenius power sums are 9,−27,−162, hence initial coefficients −9,54,−189; reciprocity gives 486,−729,729. Multiplication yields the stated cube, with L(1)=7^3=343. The named elliptic curve has seven F3-points, trace −3, and trace 3 after the quadratic base change. The matching characteristic polynomials give the asserted finite-field isogeny, not an isomorphism of polarized Jacobians. The other root eta is a conjugate and gives the same counts.
